MEMBER, KUNDAPURA, AWARDING THE COMPENSATION OF RS.6,58,640/- WITH INTEREST AT 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL THE DEPOSIT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the Insurance Company has challenged the judgment dated 10.08.2015 passed in MVC.No.806/2013 by the Senior Civil Judge & Additional MACT, Kundapura.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & Additional MACT, Kundapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 16.05.2013 at 1.30 p.m., while the petitioner was standing by the side of N.H.66 in front of Surgeon Hospital, Kundapura was hit by a goods vehicle No.KA-20-B- 3009.
After taking treatment at Surgeon Hospital, NC: 2023:KHC:41023 Kundapura he has moved the claim petition before the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.9,35,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after taking evidence, by the impugned judgment,
awarded a sum of Rs.6,58,640/- with 6% interest and fastened the liability on the insurance company to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard Sri.Pradeep.B, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Sri.K.Prasanna Sehtty,
learned counsel for the petitioner.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company that at the time of accident,
the driver of the goods vehicle did not possess valid driving license or badge to drive the heavy goods vehicle.

The Tribunal without discussing the said aspect, fastened the liability on the NC:
2023:KHC:41023 Insurance Company.
Further, learned counsel is not pressing the ground for determination of higher compensation assessed by the Tribunal and restricted his claim only with respect to the liability.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that there is a issue framed by the Tribunal throwing burden against the Insurance Company to prove that the driver did not possess the valid driving license.
On behalf of the Insurance Company, no evidence was let in.

Hence, the Branch Manager vs Santhosh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144799881/
2 Tribunal answered issue No.3 against the Insurance Company and without adducing any evidence,
it cannot be assailed.
It is further submitted that the accident took place in the year 2013.

The compensation assessed by the Tribunal by taking notional income at Rs.6,500/- is on the lower side and it ought to have been taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m. and future prospects ought to have considered NC: 2023:KHC:41023 and he sought for enhancement of compensation by exercising suo motu powers.
7.
I gave my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the materials on record.

8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injury sustained by the petitioner,
treatment taken and entitlement to claim the compensation.

Since the Insurance Company has not pressed the ground of quantum of compensation, it is not proper to exercise suo motu powers to re- determine the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the absence of the appeal by the petitioner.
Hence, this appeal is restricted only regarding the liability aspect of the Insurance Company.

9. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company along with a memo, has produced two documents,
one is notice issued to the owner of the NC: 2023:KHC:41023 vehicle under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and also reply issued by the owner to the Kundapura Town Police.

It is pertinent to note that the owner of the goods vehicle has furnished the D.L. to the Investigating Officer that, the driver of the goods vehicle as Mr.Fedrick Philip Mascarenas and the particulars of the D.L. owned by the driver as follows:
"DL/ADDL/FF1/PAGE 09, DOI 26/02/1982, RDL 3674/963/FROM 18/11/96 TO 17/11/99 FOR HEAVY GOODS VEHICLE (TR) RTO BOMBAY, NO.43351 ISSUED BY RTO UDUPI VALIED TILL 27.10.2012"
10.
As per the D.L. particulars, it is valid till 27.10.2012.
There is no material on record to show that the driver did renewed his driving license.
Until the material is placed to show to that effect, it is thus clear that the driver of the goods vehicle did not possess valid driving license including the badge at the time of accident.
However, the driver did possess NC: 2023:KHC:41023 the driving license but it was expired 6  months prior to accident.
It is clear case of violation of terms and conditions of the policy within the meaning of Section 149(2) of the MV Act, 1988.
Hence, the Insurance Company can avoid its liability but having regard to the circumstances, the petitioner cannot forced to execute the award against the owner.
The Insurance company has to deposit the compensation and recover the amount from the owner of the goods vehicle.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award Branch Manager vs Santhosh on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144799881/
3  dated 10.08.2015 passed in MVC  No.806/2013, is modified.

NC: 2023:KHC:41023 iii) The insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in the very same proceedings.
iv) Amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the tribunal.
